headline: {leaderName} signs 'Lawful Cities' order
body: Cities that receive federal funds must verify the immigration status of people using public services. The order takes effect in 30 days. Several mayors say they will sue.

headline: Agents run ID checks at three transit hubs
body: Federal agents checked identification at subway entrances in three cities this morning. 'This is a pilot, and it is working,' said agency spokesperson Craig Mullins. Commuters reported long lines and some arrests.

headline: Judge pauses clinic reporting rule
body: Judge Daniel Ramos temporarily blocked the rule requiring public clinics to report patient status, writing that it would 'keep sick people away from doctors.' {leaderName} called the ruling 'activism' and promised an appeal.

headline: Mayor Caldwell: city will join suit over 'Lawful Cities' order
body: Mayor Denise Caldwell said the city will join four others in suing over the order. 'Our libraries and clinics serve whoever walks in, and they will keep doing that,' she said. The 30-day clock keeps running while the case is heard.

headline: Clinic director: patients are waiting until it's an emergency
body: Dr. Nadia Haddad of the Fifth Street Clinic says three patients this week came in only once they needed an ambulance. 'They were afraid of the form,' she said. The agency says the reporting rule is still under appeal.

headline: {leaderName} unveils plan to clear citizenship backlog
body: The plan adds 2,000 case officers and sets a two-year target for applications older than five years. Republicans in the Senate say the cost is too high.

headline: Language-access rule signed
body: Clinics and agencies that receive federal money must now offer an interpreter on request, by phone or video when nobody on staff speaks the language. Advocates say the hard part is making sure people know to ask.

headline: Governors push back on interpreter mandate
body: Eleven governors called the language-access rule an unfunded mandate. Governor Dale Whitaker said this state will not enforce it at state-run clinics: 'Washington wrote the rule. Washington can pay for it.'

headline: City Hall opens citizenship help desk
body: Mayor Denise Caldwell opened a help desk at City Hall for residents filing under {leaderName}'s backlog plan. On the first morning the line ran out the door; staff were handing out numbered tickets by ten.

headline: Library and Grand Avenue center plan a joint health fair
body: Elm Street Library and the Grand Avenue Community Center will hold a free health fair on Saturday: blood pressure checks, flu shots and help with benefit forms. Organizers say they need volunteers who speak more than one language.

headline: Library and San José Parish Hall plan a joint health fair
body: Elm Street Library and San José Parish Hall will hold a free health fair on Saturday: blood pressure checks, flu shots and help with benefit forms. Organizers say they need volunteers who speak more than one language.

headline: Library and India Association Hall plan a joint health fair
body: Elm Street Library and the India Association Hall will hold a free health fair on Saturday: blood pressure checks, flu shots and help with benefit forms. Organizers say they need volunteers who speak more than one language.

headline: Fifth Street Clinic visits fall after ID policy
body: Staff at the Fifth Street Clinic say walk-in visits dropped by a third since the new desk policy. 'People are skipping follow-ups,' said one nurse, who asked not to be named. Director Dr. Nadia Haddad said the clinic 'will see anyone who comes in.'

headline: Library citizenship class finds a new room
body: After attendance fell, Elm Street Library moved its citizenship class to {homeCenter}, where organizers say students feel safer signing in.

headline: Police chief: officers will not run immigration checks
body: Chief Ray Kowalski told the city council that his officers will not take part in federal ID checks at transit stops. 'If people stop calling us when they're robbed, everyone is less safe,' he said. A federal spokesperson said the agency 'does not need local help.'

headline: Grand Avenue center gets a part-time social worker
body: A two-year federal grant pays for a social worker who speaks Mandarin and Cantonese to keep office hours at the Grand Avenue Community Center on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. Appointments fill a week ahead, the center says; walk-ins are seen if there is time.

headline: Parish hall adds a caseworker's office hours
body: Under a two-year federal grant, a Spanish-speaking county caseworker will keep office hours at San José Parish Hall on Wednesday afternoons: benefit forms, rent help, clinic referrals. Bring your letters, the parish office says; the line starts at noon.

headline: India Association Hall adds a caseworker's office hours
body: A two-year federal grant pays for a county caseworker who speaks Hindi and Punjabi to keep office hours at the India Association Hall one afternoon a week, starting Thursday. For other languages she will dial the county's phone interpreter line.

headline: Association questions 'cultural plaza' plan
body: The Elm Street Neighborhood Association says the proposed plaza on the Fifth Street lot was 'decided before residents were asked.' A public hearing is set for next month.

headline: Hearing on Fifth Street lot moved to library basement
body: Councilmember Kevin Tran said next month's hearing on the proposed plaza will be held at Elm Street Library 'so people can walk there.' Interpreters are available if you call the council office two days ahead. He has not said whether he supports the plan.

headline: Commuter detained at Route 9 checkpoint on his way to work
body: A warehouse worker who has lived in the city for eleven years was detained at a federal checkpoint on Route 9 at 6 a.m., driving to an early shift. His supervisor says he had not missed a day in four years. 'Checkpoints are a lawful tool, and they are working,' said agency spokesperson Craig Mullins. Neighbours have started collecting money for the family's rent.

headline: Coworkers wait for word on man held after Route 9 stop
body: A dozen coworkers from the night shift waited outside the county detention center for word on the forklift driver detained at the Route 9 checkpoint. A county legal aid lawyer says he has an application pending and 'should never have been held.' Chief Ray Kowalski said city police took no part in the checkpoint.
